skills.name: Societal impact and challenges of applied AI

note.text:
Benefits of AI: faster diagnosis, better crop yields, help for disabled people (speech-to-text), saving time on routine work, new jobs (data scientists, AI trainers).
Challenges:
• Jobs: some routine jobs may be replaced; workers need new skills.
• Privacy: AI uses large amounts of personal data, which can be misused.
• Bias and fairness: AI trained on biased data can treat groups unfairly.
• Misinformation: AI can create fake images, voices and videos (deepfakes) and convincing false text.
• Over-dependence and errors: people may trust wrong answers; AI uses a lot of energy.
Responsible use: protect personal data, check AI outputs, keep humans responsible for important decisions, follow laws and school rules.

sections.heading: The good side
sections.text:
AI can save time and lives: it helps doctors detect disease early, farmers protect crops, banks stop fraud, and people with disabilities use phones and computers (speech-to-text, text-to-speech, image description).
It also creates new jobs, such as data scientists and people who train and check AI systems.

sections.heading: The challenges
sections.text:
• Jobs: some routine jobs may disappear or change; workers need to learn new skills.
• Privacy: AI needs lots of data, often personal; it can be leaked, sold or misused.
• Bias: AI trained on unbalanced data may treat some groups unfairly.
• Fake content: deepfake videos, cloned voices and false articles can spread quickly.
• Over-trust: AI can be confidently wrong; and big AI systems use a lot of electricity.

sections.heading: Using AI responsibly
sections.text:
• Protect personal information: yours and other people's.
• Check AI answers against reliable sources.
• Do not present AI work as your own.
• Verify shocking videos before sharing them.
• Keep humans responsible for important decisions about people.

unfair treatment caused by unbalanced data or design
fake media made with AI to look real
machines doing work that people used to do

mistake.wrong: AI is always neutral and fair
mistake.right: AI can be biased if its data is biased
mistake.why: AI learns patterns from data, including unfair ones.

worked_example.problem: Give one benefit and one risk of using AI face recognition at the entrance of a school.
steps: Benefit: it can quickly check who enters, improving security.
Risk: it stores pupils' faces (personal data), which could be stolen or misused, and it may make mistakes with some faces.
worked_example.answer: Benefit: security; risk: privacy and errors

pick.q: Which is responsible use of AI tools by a student?
pick.r: Using AI to explain a topic, then checking and writing in your own words
w: Copying an AI essay and handing it in as your own
Sharing classmates' private photos with an AI app
Believing every AI answer without checking
pick.y: Use AI as a helper, honestly, and verify.

pick.q: A video of a politician saying shocking things spreads on WhatsApp. What should you do?
pick.r: Check reliable news sources before sharing; it may be a deepfake
w: Believe it because it looks real
Edit it to make it funnier

pick.q: Why should humans stay responsible for important AI decisions, such as who gets a loan?
pick.r: AI can be biased or wrong, and people must be accountable
pick.y: Accountability and fairness need human oversight.
